items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Parker grew out of Jay McShann

ctx.x: Well I don’t know, I mean a musician like Benny Carter, who wonderfully is still alive, there is a consummate genius, I mean not only is he a multi-instrumentalist, great arranger, I remember reading the fact that the BBC in their wisdom back in 1935, they hired Benny Carter to come over and they just formed a kind of BBC dance orchestra, and Benny Carter was asked to come over there and arranged for it. And I talked to some of the old time guys who are still alive who played in that band. They said Benny could…

Well it’s interesting too because those people before Parker, a lot of them, they reached a larger audience than Parker ever did. And it’s funny it’s not acknowledged, that bebop is technically demanding, and as wonderful as it was, did not have the audience that some of those before had.
